arrow-const.why: scip-typescript records a variable initialized with an arrow function or function expression as a variable (hover `const f: () => …`), not a function; fathom and universal-ctags call it a function (verified: zod packages/zod/src/v3/types.ts:5080 `const ostring = () => …`)

object-literal-method.why: scip-typescript records a contextually typed object-literal method as a reference (symbol_roles 0) to the member it implements, not a definition (verified: zod packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts:316 `transform(tx) {` is a reference to ZodType#transform().)

assigned-function.why: scip-typescript records a function assigned to a property of an untyped object (`app.use = function use(fn)`, `exports.f = …`, `module.exports = function`, `X.prototype.m = …`) as references to locals, with no definition occurrence at all (verified: expressjs/express lib/application.js:194 — symbol_roles 0 on `app`, `use` and the function expression's name)
